definition: Inarticulate means unable to express oneself clearly in words.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word inarticulate. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know inarticulate should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Face to face with his hero at the stage door, Milo went inarticulate and simply held out the record sleeve to be signed.
Halting speech limps but still gets there — it stops short of inarticulate, where the words tangle and fail to carry the meaning at all.
Speechless goes further than inarticulate: the inarticulate speaker struggles through broken phrases, while the speechless one produces nothing whatsoever.

Tongue-tied means too flustered or shy to get words out — nerves clamp the mouth shut. Inarticulate is wider and says nothing about shyness: rage, grief, or plain overload can leave a speaker inarticulate, producing broken phrases that never line up into meaning.

Incoherent talk comes out freely but does not hang together — sentences wander and never connect. An inarticulate speaker has the opposite trouble: the ideas connect perfectly well in the head, but the words refuse to line up on the way out.

Inarticulate speakers have the ideas; the words refuse to line up — in- ('not') + articulus ('small joint'): speech with the joints missing, so nothing connects.
It is not the same as speechless, which means no words come at all.
Inarticulate is the neutral word for words failing to line up — from nerves, rage, grief, or plain overload.
Speechless means nothing comes out at all; tongue-tied adds embarrassment.
The person, the speech, or even a feeling ('inarticulate longing') can all be inarticulate.

Lena Okafor could fill a whiteboard with the mathematics of her comet discovery in fifteen flawless minutes.
Live television was another matter.
Under the studio lights, with three cameras turning, she found herself suddenly inarticulate.
It was not shyness — she had lectured to packed halls for years — and her thoughts were as ordered as ever.
But the sentences kept collapsing halfway out: fragments about ice and orbits that even she could hear failing to carry what she actually knew.
The host smiled and cut to a graphic.
Driving home afterward, Lena delivered the whole explanation, perfectly, to her empty car.
